previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by worsening epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She had been on home TPN due to inability to tolerate oral intake. An MRCP was performed to rule out pseudocyst or pancreatic cancer, which showed chronic pancreatitis changes with a nearly normal secretin response and no concerning lesions. Her PICC line was found to be malpositioned and was replaced fluoroscopically. She was managed with bowel rest, TPN, IV fluids, and pain and nausea control. As symptoms improved, she was transitioned to oral hydromorphone and Phenergan suppositories, and her diet was advanced. Gabapentin was discontinued due to lack of efficacy. She was discharged home with ongoing TPN, saline infusions for dehydration, visiting nurse support, and follow-up with gastroenterology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Pt is a ___ y.o female with h.o chronic idiopathic pancreatitis, 
GERD, seasonal allergies, depression who presented with 
abdominal pain, nausea, reports of vomiting.  
.  
#abdominal pain with nausea/vomiting-Pt with h.o chronic 
idiopathic pancreatitis followed by Dr. ___ on home TPN. Pt 
reported that her presenting symptoms are typical of her prior 
flares of pancreatitis. OSH CT scan per report, no acute 
findings. LFTs/lipase/WBC normal. Symptoms likely due to chronic 
pancreatitis (recent MRCP showed findings c/w chronic 
pancreatitis, but normal secretin test), however, PUD/gastritis 
was considered to be another possibility and therefore pt 
underwent an EGD. However, this study returned normal. GI/Dr. 
___ the patient and recommended addition of 25mg 
IV phenergan Q6hr. She was initially made NPO, given TPN and 
IVF. She was given zofran, compazine and phenergan for nausea. 
IV dilaudid was initially given for pain control and then 
transitioned to PO as pt did not have any episodes of vomiting 
while admitted. Pt's pain slowly improved to near her baseline 
and she still did report nausea, but did not have any vomiting. 
Discharge nausea regimen zofran, phenergan PR and PO as prior to 
admission. Pt should continue outpt TPN as prior to admission. 
She discharge pain regimen included prior home regimen of 
lidocaine patch 100mcg daily and dilaudid up to 8mg Q4. She will 
follow up with her gastroenterologist after discharge.
.  
#GERD-continued PPI 40mg BID, EGD results as above
.  
#depression-no signs of SI-continue homed regimen of sertraline, 
bupropion, trazadone. Strongly advised to continue follow up 
with her outpatient therapist.
.  
#seasonal allergies-allergra while inpt as zyrtec non formulary.
